Description
Annapurna Labs builds the custom silicon at the heart of AWS machine learning servers, and we are hiring a software engineer to help build the Hardware Abstraction Layer (HAL) that brings these chips to life. If you love working where hardware meets software, writing the code that boots, configures, and debugs some of the largest custom silicon in the world, this is your team.
As a Software Engineer on the SoC HAL team, you will write and test C++ for the driver stack across the hardware blocks that make up our chips, learn how the silicon works from the engineers who design it, and grow your skills on a small, fast-moving team inside a large organization. No machine learning background is required (you will pick up ML concepts from colleagues if you want to). This role is based in Cupertino, CA.
Key job responsibilities
Implement, test, and maintain HAL/driver features for individual hardware blocks (for example PCIe, DDR / HBM memory, DMA, system fabric, interrupt controllers, and boot / firmware), working from designs and interfaces set by more senior engineers.
Write clean, well-tested C++ and contribute to the team's test, code-review, and continuous-deployment practices.
Debug failures that span software and silicon, with support from the team, and build an understanding of how the HAL interacts with the hardware underneath it.
Learn the hardware/software interface by partnering with RTL and design verification engineers on well-scoped questions.
Provide feature additions and bug fixes on current and prior chips.
A day in the life
A typical day moves between writing and reviewing C++ for the HAL, pairing with a teammate on a tricky bug, and learning how a hardware block works from its spec or from the engineer who designed it. You might add a feature to a driver, write tests for it, and work through code-review feedback, then dig into a failure that spans software and silicon. Your teammates are the HAL engineers you build alongside; the hardware design, verification, and firmware teams are close partners you will learn from; and your customers are the internal software teams that rely on the HAL to boot, configure, and debug the chip.
About the team
Annapurna Labs designs and deploys some of the largest custom silicon in the world, including the Trainium and Inferentia machine learning accelerators. Our SoC HAL team builds the low-level software that boots, configures, and manages these chips, sitting between the hardware and the system software that runs the server. We are a small team that works closely with hardware, holds a high engineering bar, and invests in helping engineers grow. Based in Cupertino, CA, we value mentorship, clear written design, and software that outlasts any single chip.
Minimum Qualifications
- Knowledge of programming languages such as C/C++, Python, Java or Perl
- Experience (non-internship) in professional software development, or currently enrolled in or recently completed a Bachelor's or Master's degree in computer science or a related field
- Experience with data structures, algorithms, and software design fundamentals
Preferred Qualifications
- Bachelor's degree or above in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, or related fields at time of application
- Coursework, internship, or project experience in computer architecture or operating systems
- Experience with C or C++ and object-oriented design
- Exposure to low-level, embedded, or hardware-adjacent programming
- Familiarity with testing, debugging, source control, and build processes in a team setting

Amazon Leo is Amazon's low Earth orbit satellite network. Our mission is to deliver fast, reliable internet connectivity to customers beyond the reach of existing networks. From individual households to schools, hospitals, businesses, and government agencies, Amazon Leo will serve people and organizations operating in locations without reliable connectivity.
The Leo Antenna team is looking for a Software Development Engineer who is excited to work at the intersection of large-scale data systems, Amazon Web Services cloud services, data analysis, and radio frequency hardware.
In this role, you will design and build Customer Terminal Fleet Health, the system that keeps a daily hardware health record for every customer terminal Leo operates and flags terminals whose hardware is starting to fail. You will turn telemetry from millions of satellite contacts a day into clear, trustworthy signals that tell engineers which terminals need attention and why. You do not need to come in as a radio frequency expert, but you should have a strong software engineering foundation, experience building data pipelines on Amazon Web Services, a high learning velocity, and the drive to understand phased array antennas, satellite links, and how hardware failures show up in telemetry.
This is an individual contributor software development role for someone who enjoys ambiguous technical problems, can learn across disciplines, and wants to build data systems that directly improve the reliability of a satellite network.
Export Control Requirement
Due to applicable export control laws and regulations, candidates must be a U.S. citizen or national, U.S. permanent resident (i.e., current Green Card holder), or lawfully admitted into the U.S. as a refugee or granted asylum.
Key job responsibilities
Design and build data pipelines on AWS (Step Functions, Athena, Glue, Iceberg, Lambda, S3) that process daily telemetry for the full fleet of customer terminals.
Define and own the data model for fleet health: daily per-terminal aggregates, per-satellite views, and the history engineers use to investigate a single terminal.
Partner with RF and antenna engineers to understand signal quality, temperature, reboot, and link metrics well enough to separate hardware failures from network, weather, and satellite effects.
Develop and validate the rules and models that flag failing hardware, and measure how well they work against terminals returned for repair.
Build infrastructure as code with AWS CDK, with deployment pipelines, monitoring, alarms, and integration tests that keep the system reliable.
Build dashboards and tools that let engineering and operations teams explore fleet health, compare groups of terminals, and track the effect of software and hardware changes.
Apply strong security and data-handling practices to sensitive customer and device data, including least-privilege access, encryption, and privacy controls.
Collaborate with data platform and customer terminal software teams to onboard new data sources and improve the telemetry the system depends on.
Write high-quality, maintainable code and documentation that other engineers and teams across Leo can build on.
A day in the life
You may start the day reviewing the overnight fleet health run, checking that every data source arrived and looking at which terminals were newly flagged. You might then sit down with antenna and radio frequency engineers on a group of terminals whose signal quality dropped, digging through the data together to decide whether it points to failing hardware, a software release, or something outside the terminal.
Later, you may meet with the data platform and customer terminal software teams to onboard a new telemetry source, then write the infrastructure and pipeline code that brings it into the daily run with tests and alarms in place. You might finish the day with field operations, comparing the watch list against recent hardware returns to see which failures the system flagged early, which it missed, and what each returned terminal can teach the rules.
Across all of it, your work helps engineers spot failing hardware before customers notice and measure the effect of software and hardware changes across the fleet. This role requires curiosity, technical depth, and the ability to move between data engineering, cloud infrastructure, and hardware context. You will not just write code; you will help define how Leo understands the health of every terminal in its fleet.
About the team
The Leo Customer Terminal Software Team supports the devices that connect customers to the Leo satellite network. We provide embedded application software and the underlying Linux system software for these terminals. We work hand in hand with hardware, product, and operations teams to deliver a great experience for our customers. As Leo moves toward full-scale production and global deployment, this is a compelling time to join and help shape how millions of people get online for the first time.

We're seeking a Sr.Software Development Engineer with deep storage expertise to architect, build, and operate the high-performance storage infrastructure that accelerates silicon development at Annapurna Labs. In this role, you'll own the storage platforms—spanning Amazon FSx for NetApp ONTAP, FSx for Lustre, and S3—that enable chip design teams to iterate faster, run regressions more efficiently, and bring transformative custom silicon to market.
Key job responsibilities
You will design, deploy, and operate high-performance storage platforms—Amazon FSx for NetApp ONTAP (Gen1/Gen2) and FSx for Lustre—optimized for EDA and HPC workloads. This includes managing NFS exports, ONTAP SVMs, intelligent tiering (FabricPool), snapshot policies, SnapMirror replication, and quota enforcement across multi-tenant environments. You'll deploy all storage infrastructure using AWS CDK, architect cross-VPC and multi-account solutions via Transit Gateway and Route 53 private hosted zones, enable EFA for high-throughput Lustre access, and manage data synchronization using DataSync and S3 integrations. You'll build a Storage as a Service platform with self-service provisioning, defined SLOs, cost attribution, and automated lifecycle management that enables teams to consume storage without deep specialization.
You will build monitoring and observability for storage health, utilization, and cost trends, and establish incident response processes for storage-related failures. You'll continuously evaluate and adopt new AWS storage features—Gen2 scale-out, NVMe-over-TCP, enhanced backup performance—to keep the platform at the leading edge. You'll profile I/O patterns across EDA workloads, tune file system configurations for optimal performance, and partner with silicon design and verification teams to proactively scale capacity and mentor others on storage best practices.
A day in the life
You might start your day reviewing storage utilization dashboards and tiering efficiency reports, identifying file systems approaching capacity thresholds or workloads that would benefit from tier migration. Mid-morning, you could be collaborating with a verification team to provision a new FSx for Lustre file system optimized for their regression suite—sizing it based on their I/O profiles, enabling EFA access, and deploying it through your CDK pipeline.
In the afternoon, you might be building the next iteration of your Storage as a Service platform—adding automated quota enforcement for a new team onboarding, implementing a snapshot policy that aligns with their project milestones, or extending cross-VPC access to a new account. You'll review pull requests for CDK constructs, investigate a DataSync job that stalled, and discuss FSx ONTAP Gen2 migration plans with your team.
Throughout the day, you'll balance immediate customer needs—expanding a volume for a team blocked on disk space, troubleshooting NFS mount latency—with longer-term platform investments like evaluating intelligent tiering policies or prototyping NVMe-over-TCP access patterns. You'll engage with AWS service teams on feature requests and roadmap alignment, ensuring Annapurna Labs gets the most from the storage platform.
About the team
At Annapurna Labs, your storage infrastructure work directly enables breakthrough innovations in custom silicon that power AWS and transform industries. The EDA Cloud Infrastructure team builds and operates the compute, storage, and networking platforms that hundreds of chip designers and verification engineers depend on daily. We offer the resources and scale of AWS with the innovation culture and technical depth of a focused silicon team.
If you're passionate about storage systems, thrive on building platforms that make complex infrastructure simple for others, and want to see your work accelerate the next generation of AWS silicon—we want to hear from you.

You will own major features and services across two connected products that deliver specialist expertise to the AWS field:
- AWS Specialist Agent (ASA) – A production multi-agent system that gives field teams deep technical expertise across all AWS domains on demand. - Build and maintain evaluation test sets, prompts, and guardrails. Use evaluation results to decide what ships, and help define the quality bar for agent responses.

On your on-call weeks, you handle alarms, lead the fix for the root cause, and turn what you learn into operational improvements.

We are engineers, applied scientists, and product managers. Engineers own their services from design through on-call. SDE IIs act as technical owners of major components and help senior engineers set the team's technical direction.

The Resilience Infrastructure and Solutions (RIS) organization makes good on that promise, driving higher availability for AWS customers through fewer and shorter operational events. We build the services and programs that detect, mitigate, and recover from failures, from a single impaired Availability Zone to a full Region. Join our Robotics Development and Packaging Innovation Experiences team as a Software Development Engineer and help shape the future of sustainable packaging at Amazon. You'll design and deploy large-scale systems that decide which products get tested, collect and verify the physical attributes of items, and turn that data into packaging decisions that reduce waste, lower our cost to serve, and support Amazon's commitment to the Climate Pledge. Our products and programs are public facing, so you'll have a unique opportunity to shape what customers experience on every order.
As a Software Development Engineer on our team, you'll focus on building intelligent packaging deterministic workflows and large-scale platforms that power our packaging operations worldwide. These systems process hundreds of millions of products every day, across hundreds of fulfillment centers and every customer order. That work drives hundreds of millions of dollars in savings, reduces packaging waste and damage, and puts sustainable packaging choices in front of millions of customers. You'll own the services that decide which products to test, the tools fulfillment center associates and test labs rely on to test, inspect, and escalate packaging issues, and the customer-facing packaging experiences across the product detail page, cart, and checkout, including concealment for items whose packaging could reveal what's inside. You'll participate in code reviews with peers, mentor junior engineers as they grow their skills, and contribute to discussions that shape our technical strategy. Beyond individual contributions, you'll help establish best practices that ensure quality across our infrastructure and production services, which form the backbone of our packaging engines and support our Climate Pledge and sustainability initiatives.
Your work will shape how millions of packages ship every day, with every decision explainable down to a single product. You will build the source of truth for how Amazon understands the physical world of its products: what they're made of, how they hold up in transit, and how they should ship. You will design systems where every attribute carries its full history, including its source, confidence, and the test or model that produced it, so teams across Amazon can build on it with confidence. You will drive intelligent prioritization that puts testing effort where it creates the most value, and help build a platform where new packaging programs, such as flexible and automated packaging, launch quickly through configuration. We are seeking an engineer who is a true owner: hands-on, comfortable with ambiguity, and excited to define new technology that will be used by Amazon fulfillment and packaging services around the world.
Key job responsibilities
- Design, develop, test, and deploy item packaging intelligence workflows and platforms that serve our worldwide customer base
- Partner with product leaders, operations, and cross-functional teams to influence packaging roadmap decisions and define technical strategy aligned with sustainability goals
- Build and maintain core infrastructure, production services, and tools that support fulfillment centers, test labs, and field operations
- Deliver customer-facing packaging experiences across the product detail page, cart, and checkout. Make sure eligibility and concealment data shows up accurately, run controlled experiments, and resolve customer-reported issues at the root cause
- Build toward a unified, traceable item attribute store and configurable prioritization that lets new packaging programs launch without new engineering effort
- Drive system architecture decisions and establish best practices that enable code quality, reliability, and scalability across our software systems
- Coach and support junior engineers in their technical growth and help them develop their skills in building large-scale distributed systems
